title: bug: Codex/Gemini/Grok seats can never release a contested hold, yet MOE_CONTESTED_HELD's remedy tells them a Serena editor will
description:
Filed by the governor from a stall observed on 2026-10-30.

What happened:
- task-2cf1c6be's Codex seat (worker-262588d0, session 09:40:34Z) followed the MOE_CONTESTED_HELD remedy. It re-edited scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs with Serena replace_in_files, but completion 8f62fa0f still held the path.
- QA rejected the row for a delivery gap: the code was fine, but its bytes were never committed.
- The R11e2 fix round (worker-6e57c4f8, also Codex) hit the same wall. That file was dirty at the seat's pre-flight, so the seat can't land its TC6 rows at all.

Root cause: a documented wrapper limit. Per docs/CONFIGURATION.md "Session touch evidence" and TROUBLESHOOTING "Current witness limit", only one-shot Claude stream-json editing events feed the TOOL tier. Codex, Gemini, Grok and interactive Claude sessions never produce a witness, Serena edits included. Yet the remedy text says otherwise. It tells every seat "edit each held path with a wrapper-observed editing tool (Claude Edit/Write or a Serena editor, not a shell write)", in:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh:4251;
- scripts/moe-agent.ps1:3794;
- packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.ts:24 (the #governors alert);
- the docs/MCP_SERVER.md:805 row.
A Codex seat that obeys still gets held. That costs a QA reject round each time. On the hot files (local-runner.test.mjs, moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, postflight.{sh,ps1}) it can push a chain head toward the reopen cap.

Second defect, same area: the label `held=<path>(task-<peer>)` names the peer entry's first claimant in id order (taskIds[0]). That may not be the peer that caused the hold. At 8f62fa0f it named idle, dependency-gated R11e (task-001d8ab3), while the contester that was actually live was R11e2 (task-1e7f5a2d, just reassigned). QA was misled into suggesting a governor archive R11e as "stale".

Fix, in parity across sh and ps1:
(1) Make the remedy honest about who can release a hold. One-shot Claude Edit/Write and Serena editors count. A Codex, Gemini, Grok or interactive Claude session cannot release it by editing. Its routes are: a one-shot Claude session of the same task touches the path, or a later session of the task whose pre-flight saw the path clean while every contesting peer is idle, or the peer completes. Update the wrapper lines, recordCommit.ts, MCP_SERVER/TROUBLESHOOTING, and the exact-string assertions in scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1} and recordCommit.test.ts.
(2) Make the held= label name the peer(s) that caused the hold: editing peers first, then active ones, then the rest. Check first what task-01f37ac6 (per-path peer lists from get_commit_scope, which this row depends on) already changes here, and build on it.
(3) Candidate for a SPIDR split if it exceeds the size caps: harvest TOOL witnesses for `codex exec` seats from `codex exec --json` JSONL events. That means apply_patch file changes plus successful Serena editing MCP calls, under the same success-only rules as the claude stream parser, so Codex seats can land contested paths they edited.

Keep the policy itself unchanged: never weaken attribution.contested.
definitionOfDone: The MOE_CONTESTED_HELD remedy text (moe-agent.sh, moe-agent.ps1, recordCommit.ts alert, docs/MCP_SERVER.md and TROUBLESHOOTING.md) no longer tells a seat that cannot produce a TOOL witness to use a Serena editor. It states which sessions can release a hold and the alternative routes, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.

held=<path>(task-<peer>) names the contesting peer that caused the hold, editing or active peers before idle plan-only claimants, proven by a postflight.{sh,ps1} row with an idle first claimant and an active second peer.
scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1} and packages/moe-daemon recordCommit tests pass with the updated exact strings; attribution.contested semantics are unchanged.

Either codex exec seats harvest TOOL witnesses from --json events (with postflight rows proving that a Codex-edited contested path lands), or that work is split into its own task and named in the completion summary.
